declared.title: Wanting to be Happy Fosters Happiness by Promoting Savoring: A Daily Diary Study
declared.foundIn: reports/chasing-happiness/counter-evidence.md (card 8); Crossref search « happiness goals savoring intense happiness daily diary Pavani » (2026-11-22)

population: 100 French women aged 19 to 45, mostly highly educated, 31 evenings of diary (author's PDF)

findings.text: Women who wanted more to be happy had more often intense happiness, partly because they savored good moments more

support.sentence: First, as expected, at the between-individual level, individuals with higher happiness goals were more likely to experience intense happiness, partly because they engaged more in savoring.
support.readBy: writer agent, 2026-11-22: abstract of the author's PDF on HAL (hal-05462372); none in Crossref, Europe PMC, OpenAlex

findings.text: On evenings when a woman wanted more than usual to be happy the next day, she was more likely to have intense happiness that day, partly through savoring

support.sentence: Second, as expected, at the within-individual level, when an individual displayed higher happiness goals for tomorrow than usual, the individual was more likely to experience intense happiness during the next day than usual, partly due to stronger engagement in savoring.
support.readBy: writer agent, 2026-11-22: abstract of the author's PDF on HAL (hal-05462372); none in Crossref, Europe PMC, OpenAlex

limits: women only, one country, mostly highly educated
association over days, never a manipulation
happiness of the day rated by one item each evening
